securityFindings.assetTrustBoundary: Supabase pgAudit object-audit role -> Vault decrypted view and privileged public/private tables
securityFindings.affectedVersionConfiguration: Postgres 17.11; pgaudit 17.1; capital_ai_security_auditor NOLOGIN NOINHERIT NOBYPASSRLS; postgres membership SET FALSE; pgAudit.role=capital_ai_security_auditor
securityFindings.attackPath: Audit role intentionally holds SELECT on vault.decrypted_secrets and vault.secrets, and DML on user_provider_connections, subscriptions, owner credential/challenge/session tables to select logged command classes. Exposure would require privilege escalation/misassignment or privileged SQL path.
securityFindings.exploitability: DIRECT_UNPRIVILEGED_PATH_NOT_OBSERVED; role has NOLOGIN, postgres membership inherit=false and set=false; residual privilege/role-membership/configuration-drift risk.
securityFindings.impact: If role becomes assumable or privileges bypass intended boundaries, decrypted BYOK and account authority integrity are impacted.
evidence: Live pg_roles/pg_auth_members schema usage and has_table_privilege SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE readbacks 2026-10-11T22:52Z
securityFindings.mitigation: Preserve intended pgAudit object logging; regularly recheck NOLOGIN, role memberships/SET eligibility, direct PUBLIC/schema rights; least-privilege review of logged columns and selected commands. Do NOT blindly REVOKE audit grants as they configure object-log coverage.
